title: DelegationRevocationInclusionReceipt (v1)
description: The relay's signed statement that it recorded one DelegationRevocation at `seq` (standing-delegation@1.3). With a later set attestation from the same relay key covering `seq` but lacking the record, proves relay self-contradiction (omission) — never independent acceptance (same signer). Canonicalization: JCS (RFC 8785). Signature: Ed25519 over canonicalJson(body minus signature), base64url. See spec/standing-delegation-v1.md §5.3.

spec.description: Artifact discriminator (domain separation from every other relay-signed artifact).

relay_public_key.description: The relay's Ed25519 public key, hex-encoded (64 lowercase). Consumers compare it to the key they pin.

revocation_signature.description: The recorded DelegationRevocation's `signature`, verbatim — the record's identity (the relay is idempotent on it).

seq.description: The receipt sequence number the relay assigned to the record. A later set attestation from the same relay key with `seq_high_water >= seq` MUST carry the record at this seq; one that does not proves the relay contradicted itself.

received_at.description: Unix ms, the relay's receipt clock.

suite.description: Cryptosuite identifier. Always `motebit-jcs-ed25519-b64-v1`: JCS (RFC 8785), Ed25519, base64url signature, hex public keys.

signature.description: Base64url-encoded Ed25519 signature over `canonicalJson(body)` (this object minus `signature`), by `relay_public_key`. Verify against the relay key the consumer PINS — the embedded key alone proves nothing.
